info.bio:
• Named Captain of the Fleet for the 2025-26 season. Served as Alternate Captain for the 2024 and 2024-25 seasons.

  • Signed a two-year contract extension with Boston on Aug. 4, 2025, through the 2027-28 season.

  • Keller scored two goals, one unassisted, in the 3rd period of the Fleet’s first matchup of the season against New York, helping the Fleet defeat the Sirens 4-2. Her performance earned her the first star of the game honor.

  • Recorded a four-game point streak from Dec. 27, 2024 – Jan. 5, 2025, earning at least one assist in each game for the Fleet.

  • Registered a season-high six hits in the Fleet’s 3-2 win against the Charge on Feb. 20, 2025. Ranked 2nd in the PWHL in hits (49).

  • During the inaugural season, Keller ranked eighth overall in the PWHL with a plus-minus rating of 9. Also finished 18th overall in the PWHL in regular season points with 16 in 24 games.

  • Top three finalist for 2024 PWHL Defender of the Year.

  • Recorded her first PWHL goal in Boston’s inaugural game against Minnesota on January 3, 2024.

  • Represented the U.S. in two Olympic Winter Games (gold in 2018, silver in 2022).

  • Played in nine International IIHF Women’s World Championship with the U.S. Women’s National Team (gold in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2019, 2023, 2025; silver in 2021, 2022, 2024), as well as four Four Nations Cups (finishing 1s in 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2nd in 2014).

  • Played in the 2014 IIHF Under-18 Women’s World Championship (silver), three Under-22 Series vs. Canada (2014, 2015, 2016) and the 2013 Under-18 Series vs. Canada.

  • U.S. Women’s National Team alternate captain for 2023-24 seasons. 

  • Represented the U.S. at international events, including the 2021 My Why Tour, presented by Toyota, 2019-20 Rivalry Series, and The Time Is Now Tour, presented by Toyota (2017). 

  • At Boston College, she set the record for single-season points and goals scored for a defender and held the record for conference career and single-season points, goals and assists by a defender. 

  • Won the Cammi Granato Award as Hockey East’s top player and earned First-Team Hockey East honors in her junior year at Boston College. 

  • College awards and honors: Hockey East Player of the Year for the 2018-2019 season, First Team All-American (2016-2017), First Team All-American (2015-2016), Voted Hockey East Best Defensemen (2015-2016), Hockey East First Team All-Star (2015-2016), Hockey East All-Star First Team (2014-2015), Hockey East All-Rookie Team (2014-2015).
